city.name: Queenstown
city.description: Queenstown on Lake Wakatipu from open data: LINZ's 1 m LiDAR terrain and roofs under its 2026 aerial photos, the Skyline Gondola to Bob's Peak and the TSS Earnslaw at Steamer Wharf, lit by the real sun.

tour.title: Queenstown from Bob's Peak
tour.text: {buildings} buildings on LINZ's 1 m LiDAR terrain, every roof measured from the 2021 surface model, under the 2026 aerial photos. The Remarkables across the lake are LINZ's national 8 m DEM under its 10 m satellite mosaic.

tour.title: The bay from the Fernhill side
tour.text: Queenstown Bay, the Gardens peninsula and Frankton Arm from the hillside above Lake Esplanade, with the Remarkables beyond. The Earnslaw sails from Steamer Wharf.

tour.title: The Skyline Gondola
tour.text: {landmark:skyline_gondola.length_m} m up the face of Bob's Peak and {landmark:skyline_gondola.rise_m} m up from Brecon Street. The line and its stations are OpenStreetMap's; its six towers, three masts and three portals, are placed and measured from their shadows in LINZ's 2026 aerial photographs.

tour.title: Steamer Wharf
tour.text: The TSS Earnslaw's berth, where she has sailed from since 1912. In the game she steams across Frankton Arm.

tour.title: Sun on the lakefront
tour.text: Marine Parade Reserve is in direct sun for {sun:Marine Parade Reserve|6-21|12:00}% of its area at noon on the winter solstice, under the hill to the north-west.

frame.units: m, z = m above Lake Wakatipu

shore.encoding: r: 128 + 2 x signed distance to the shoreline (m, water positive); g: sand; b: rock

waves.note: A light south-westerly down the lake's reach from Cecil Peak to the town, chosen values, not a measurement. The lake is mostly glassy at dawn and ruffled by afternoon.

seawall.note: Queenstown's lake front: grey schist rubble walls and concrete along Marine Parade and the wharves; the lake rises and falls by about a metre with the seasons, not with a tide.

trees.note: Species are not mapped; the mix is a guess at Queenstown's planting: Douglas fir and other conifers on Bob's Peak and in the Gardens (drawn as the shared pine and sugi), oaks, sycamores, poplars and willows (drawn as the elm and maple) on the streets and the lake front, and a few eucalypts. The woods on Ben Lomond's lower slopes are wilding conifers.

sources.lidar_heights: LINZ Otago - Queenstown LiDAR 1m DSM (2021): the median roof inside each footprint the survey misses

woods.encoding: r: ground cover under the canopy (0-255), g: canopy height x 8 (m), b: a footway under the canopy, a: in a wood or park
